title.en: Hear both sides of a debate
title.es: Escuchar las dos posturas de un debate

es: Reconocer en un debate escolar dónde el hablante concede un punto, dónde lo rebate y dónde concluye.

vocabulary.es: te doy la razón en que, admito que
una norma que se aplica a todos por igual

teaching.en: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency, but the office already has a landline for pupils.
teaching.es: Es cierto que un celular es un salvavidas en una emergencia, pero la oficina ya tiene un teléfono fijo para los alumnos.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly abre la concesión; el but posterior abre la refutación, que es lo que el hablante defiende de verdad.
segments: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency,
but the office already has a landline for pupils.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency, but the office already has a landline for pupils.

teaching.en: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain, but its claim to raise results does not hold water.
teaching.es: Reconozco que una prohibición total es fácil de explicar, pero su pretensión de mejorar los resultados no se sostiene.
teaching.explanationEs: I concede that… cede un punto y but abre lo que se defiende. Hold water = resistir un examen: casi siempre se usa en negativa.
segments: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain,
but its claim to raise results does not hold water.
teaching.audioText: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain, but its claim to raise results does not hold water.

teaching.en: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.
teaching.es: Es una preocupación válida, y te doy la razón en que los celulares distraen de las clases; dicho esto, una norma para todos por igual castiga a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: I grant you that… concede con tono generoso; that said es un giro suave, parecido a «aun así».
segments: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones
distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.
teaching.audioText: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.

teaching.en: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.
teaching.es: Algunos alumnos sí usan el celular con sensatez; sin embargo, una sola norma para todos es más fácil de aplicar y más difícil de discutir.
teaching.explanationEs: Nevertheless va detrás del punto concedido (some pupils do…) y abre lo que el hablante prefiere defender.
segments: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule
for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.
teaching.audioText: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.

teaching.en: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones in bags during lessons but allow them at break.
teaching.es: Para concluir, y sopesándolo todo, guardaría los celulares en las mochilas durante las clases, pero los permitiría en el recreo.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude anuncia el cierre; on balance indica que has sopesado los dos lados antes de decidir.
segments: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones
in bags during lessons but allow them at break.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones in bags during lessons but allow them at break.

teaching.en: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection first, then take issue with it calmly.
teaching.es: Un orador justo concederá primero la objeción más fuerte y luego discrepará de ella con calma.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceder lo más fuerte del otro lado da credibilidad; take issue with = discrepar de, poner objeciones a.
segments: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection
first, then take issue with it calmly.
teaching.audioText: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection first, then take issue with it calmly.

prompt.es: Localiza la concesión: ¿qué reconoce la hablante antes de girar?

choices.text: That a ringing phone can pull attention away from a lesson.
That a locker system deserves a one-term trial in this school.
That phones ruin concentration in every lesson, as some teachers claim.

feedback.es: La concesión llega antes de «That said»: admite que una pantalla que vibra distrae; el ensayo con taquillas es lo que propone ella y arruinar la concentración es lo que alegan otros.

hint.es: La concesión es lo que admite antes del giro, no lo que defiende después.

origin.text: Some teachers argue that phones ruin concentration, and I grant you that a ringing phone can distract from a lesson. That said, our school has never tried a simple locker system, so nobody can claim it failed. On balance, I would like to see it tested for one term.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te doy la razón: puede serlo, pero la oficina tiene un teléfono gratuito.»

feedback.es: I grant you that… es la fórmula de concesión generosa; concede no admite «you» detrás.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «admitir, dar la razón»; empieza por g.

origin.text: Some pupils say a phone is a lifeline after dark. I ___ you that it can be, but the office phone is free to use.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es un punto válido, pero la norma sigue en pie.»

answer.text: That is a valid point but the rule still stands

feedback.es: La concesión (valid point) va primero y el giro con but introduce lo que se defiende.

hint.es: Primero la concesión, después but y tu postura.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede la hablante sobre las clases con celular.

choices.text: That a dictionary check is a poor reason to allow phones.
That some pupils do waste whole lessons staring at their own screens.
That a traffic-light system would be unfair to teachers.

feedback.es: «I accept that some pupils stare at their screens…» es la concesión; «Even so» abre la refutación y el semáforo es su propuesta.

origin.audio: Ms Reyes says phones should stay in bags all day. I see where she is coming from, and I accept that some pupils stare at their screens for an entire lesson. Even so, a blanket rule punishes those who use a phone to check a dictionary. She could try a traffic-light system instead, with green for research and red for silence.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con la función que cumple.

pairs: Admittedly, the rule is easy to explain
That said, it is hard to enforce
On balance, I would keep it
That argument does not hold water
One phone rang during the test

feedback.es: Cada marcador cumple un papel: Admittedly concede, that said gira, on balance cierra, hold water descarta y one phone rang ilustra.

pairs: Admittedly, the rule is easy to explain
That said, it is hard to enforce
On balance, I would keep it
That argument does not hold water
One phone rang during the test

prompt.es: ¿Qué defiende realmente Tom en este resumen de su intervención?

choices.text: That phones in emergencies are so important that no rule should limit them.
That pupils who use phones sensibly should be punished along with the rest.
That the ban is reasonable because pupils can already phone home from school.

feedback.es: Tom concede el valor del celular en una emergencia, pero lo que defiende es que la prohibición es razonable porque ya existe otra vía.

origin.text: Tom's speech opened with a concession: phones do let pupils reach home in an emergency. He then turned sharply, pointing out that the same pupils already have access to the school office. His closing line was more cautious, suggesting only that the ban should be reviewed after one term.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué concede Leo antes de su giro.

choices.text: That a newcomer might depend on a translation app.
That most pupils use translation apps to cheat in tests.
That Mia had used a translation app herself at school.
That Mia's point deserved more attention than it had received.

feedback.es: La concesión es la generosidad inicial hacia el punto de Mia: un alumno recién llegado puede depender de la aplicación; lo demás es una generalización, un dato no mencionado o una opinión que Leo no expresa.

origin.audio: At Tuesday's debate, Leo argued for keeping phones in bags. He opened generously: Mia's point about translation apps was fair, he said, and he could see how a pupil new to the country might rely on one. Even so, he went on, the same app can write a whole essay in seconds, and teachers cannot tell the difference from across the room. He did not claim that every pupil cheats; he said only that a rule has to work for the pupils who do. On balance, he thought a ban in tests and a free hand in practice lessons was the honest middle ground, although he admitted the school might struggle to enforce it.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué actitud muestra Leo hacia su propia propuesta final?

choices.text: He presents it as a perfect answer that leaves nothing more to discuss.
He offers a fair compromise but admits it may be hard to apply.
He proposes it reluctantly and would drop it the moment teachers object.
He sees it as a fair compromise that most teachers will gladly welcome.

feedback.es: Leo llama «honest middle ground» a su propuesta, pero admite que aplicarla puede costar: actitud de compromiso realista, no de certeza ni de desgana.

origin.audio: At Tuesday's debate, Leo argued for keeping phones in bags. He opened generously: Mia's point about translation apps was fair, he said, and he could see how a pupil new to the country might rely on one. Even so, he went on, the same app can write a whole essay in seconds, and teachers cannot tell the difference from across the room. He did not claim that every pupil cheats; he said only that a rule has to work for the pupils who do. On balance, he thought a ban in tests and a free hand in practice lessons was the honest middle ground, although he admitted the school might struggle to enforce it.

prompt.es: Completa: «La directora estaba dispuesta a conceder que la norma era confusa.»

feedback.es: Concede that… es la colocación natural para reconocer un punto ajeno sin cambiar la postura; los sinónimos admit o accept también encajan.

origin.text: The head teacher was prepared to ___ that the old rule had been unclear. She would not, however, drop it completely, and she asked the council to give it one more term.

prompt.es: Escribe una concesión y una refutación sobre traductores en exámenes.

answer.text: I grant you that a translation app can help newcomers; that said, in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the words.
accepted: I grant you that a translation app can help newcomers; that said, in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the words.
Admittedly, a translation app helps pupils who are new to the country; nevertheless, in an exam it would be unfair to those who have studied the words.
I concede that an app can help newcomers, but in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the vocabulary.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta concede con una fórmula (I grant you, admittedly, I concede) y gira después hacia la postura propia.

origin.text: Concede que un traductor ayuda a los alumnos recién llegados y rebate que en un examen sería injusto para quienes han estudiado las palabras.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe Sara este correo a la dirección?

choices.text: To drop the council's objection now that she understands the rule.
To accuse the staff of ignoring what the survey of pupils clearly shows.
To ask for a delay so that the council's findings can be considered.
To propose that the ban apply at break but not in lessons, as pupils prefer.

feedback.es: Sara reconoce la postura del centro, pero su petición es esperar a los resultados completos: busca aplazar, no retirar ni acusar.

origin.text: Dear Head Teacher, thank you for meeting the pupil council. I understand why you want a single rule, and I do not doubt that staff are under pressure. All the same, our survey suggests that most pupils would accept a ban in lessons but not at break. I would therefore ask you to hold off on the outright ban until we have shared the full results next week.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, el argumento a favor de la prohibición no se sostiene.»

answer.text: On balance the case for a ban does not hold water
accepted: On balance the case for a ban does not hold water
The case for a ban does not hold water on balance

feedback.es: On balance abre una valoración global y does not hold water descarta el argumento.

prompt.es: Completa: «La última razón, francamente, no se sostenía.»

feedback.es: Hold water (o hold up) describe un argumento que resiste el examen; Carlos debió conceder que el cuarto no lo hacía.

origin.text: Carlos listed four reasons for the ban. The first three were strong; the last one, frankly, did not hold ___. He should have conceded as much.
